reference: Torres, Claret, Pavlovski & Dotter 2015, ApJ 807, 26, Table 3

evolutionary_track_source.metallicity_note: Z=0.019 (Y=0.273) is the paper's own identified solar-composition value (Sect. 2: "almost identical to the Z=0.01886 favoured by Anders & Grevesse 1989"), appropriate for this Sun-like system.
evolutionary_track_source.status_note: Standardized on 2026-08-29 as this project's default evolutionary-track grid, for direct comparability with the Al-Wardat SED-fitting literature this system benchmarks against (which consistently uses Girardi 2000). Code-level integration (pyseshat.evolution.parsers.girardi2000, pyseshat.evolution.grids's "girardi2000" model) is in place, but no real Girardi (2000) numeric track/isochrone data has been sourced into this repository yet -- confirmed network blocker (VizieR, CDS FTP, and the Padova CMD legacy interface are all unreachable from this development environment's egress, including the linked user device; see docs/guide/evolutionary_checks.md's 2026-08-29 entry). No evolutionary consistency check has therefore been run against this system's fitted/literature (Teff, R) yet -- this is an open item, not a result, and no age/mass/evolutionary-stage number should be attributed to this system from this repository until that data is obtained.
evolutionary_track_source.prior_grid: None -- no evolutionary-track grid (Girardi, PARSEC, or otherwise) had ever been run against this system before this entry; PARSEC parsing infrastructure existed in the codebase but with zero bundled data and zero benchmark wiring.

data_provenance: SYNTHETIC measurements: combined-light magnitudes are generated from this file's own literature Teff/R/logg via PySeshat's own synthetic_binary_magnitudes(), plus Gaussian noise at an ASSUMED 0.03 mag representative precision -- a forward-model self-consistency check (does fit_photometry recover known input Teff/R/E(B-V) from data generated by PySeshat's own model), not a comparison to independently-observed sky photometry. See scripts/build_joint_benchmarks.py module docstring.

metallicity.source: nearest available CK04 grid point (ckp00); literature [Fe/H]=-0.04 (Torres et al. 2015) is not itself used -- only the solar-metallicity grid is downloaded for this project

radius_prior_note: 10% relative sigma Gaussian prior on each component's radius, tied to the literature value -- same convention as the other four Al-Wardat systems.
